To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Na+ and Cl- exclusion are two independent salt tolerance mechanisms, 2) Na+ stress reduces K+ and Ca+ uptake and photosynthesis, 3) Cl- stress reduces photosynthetic capacity and chlorophyll content, and 4) the importance of different mechanisms of damage depends on the growth system.
Na+ and CI– ions have additive effects on growth reduction of barley plants under salinity stress, and the mechanisms of Na+ and CI- exclusion are independent of each other.
NaCl is more toxic to plants than either Na+ or Cl– alone, and that the relative toxicity of NaCl, Na+, and Cl– varies with the growth system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of NaCl and its individual components on the growth and physiological responses of four contrasting barley genotypes.
the effects of specific ion toxicities and the mechanisms by which they reduce the growth of crop plants.
the effects of NaCl on the growth of barley in saline soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of high salinity on plant growth are mainly additive of the toxic effects of high Na+ and Cl concentrations.
NaCl stress reduced growth mainly by reducing the photosynthetic efficiency, and that the reduction in photosynthesis was mainly due to the toxic effects of both Na+ and Cl− ions.
the additive effects of Na+ toxicity and Cl– toxicity are the main factors that limit plant growth under salinity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
salinity damage in barley plants grown in saline soils involves both the Na+ toxicity and Cl– toxicity, and the extent of damage is determined by both Na+ and Cl concentrations in soil solutions.

the effects of salinity on barley growth and photosynthesis are mainly caused by Na+ toxicity, but Cl– toxicity can also contribute significantly to the reduction in barley growth under saline conditions.
NaCl stress reduced growth and photosynthesis mainly by the additive effects of Na+ toxicity on stomatal conductance, and the non-stomatal toxicity of Cl– on photosynthetic efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Na+ and chloride (Cl-) ions have different toxic effects on plant growth, and that the effects of NaCl stress are mainly additive of the individual ion toxicities.
the mechanisms of salt damage are not only different in different genotypes, but they are also different between soil and solution cultures.
NaCl is more damaging to barley than either Na+ or Cl– alone, and that Na+ and NaCl are more damaging in soil than solution culture, whereas Cl– is equally damaging in both systems.
